question: Should `openclaw/crabbox` own, release, and marketplace-advertise the Herdr plugin as a first-party integration?
rationale: The implementation adds a permanent external-product package, hidden CLI contract, release-order dependency, documentation surface, and repository topic requirement; code review cannot determine that ownership commitment without maintainer intent.

options.title: Own the integration
options.body: Keep the plugin in this repository, repair current-main dispatch, require upgrade and live proof, and release the manifest and compatible CLI together.

options.title: Publish separately
options.body: Move the Herdr manifest and scripts to a dedicated integration repository while retaining only a documented stable Crabbox CLI interface if maintainers want to support it.

options.title: Decline first-party support
options.body: Close the proposal without adding a repository-owned Herdr package or hidden compatibility contract.

recommendation.title: Own the integration
recommendation.body: Keep the plugin in this repository, repair current-main dispatch, require upgrade and live proof, and release the manifest and compatible CLI together.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history shows the strongest ownership signal across the CLI and release-facing repository surface.
